newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 19.

text.p: There are 104 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES said that according to the Basic Law, the Independent Commission Against Corruption should be able to remain independent after the handover. It said that after July, the fight against corruption would be more complicated and would require the future Chief Executive and ICAC officials to have great courage to keep Hong Kong society clean.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD said some people believed that Governor Chris Patten would pick on anything to "stir things up" in the closing weeks of British rule, and in picking on the likely name change of the Independent Commission Against Corruption, Patten appeared to prove these people right. According to the Basic Law, there would be no change to the function of the ICAC, as far as accountability was concerned, the paper said.

-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS said news that the advance party of the People's Liberation Army's Hong Kong garrison would not be armed showed that PLA officials knew the situation in the territory well. The paper said that if the PLA garrison continued to take such a friendly attitude towards to territory, Hong Kong people would not harbour any fears about it.
